D021-D005_h001.question: Lately, I’ve been constantly shedding weight. Every morning, I step on the scale with a knot in my stomach, terrified of seeing that number go up, even by an ounce. The thought of gaining weight paralyzes me, and I can literally feel my own perception of my body changing in real-time. I’ve cut out all carbs and fats, which I know sounds extreme, but it's the only way I can stay in control. My wife says I'm wasting away, but I just see myself as making progress. I often find myself thinking people are secretly trying to sabotage my diet by offering me food. I know, logically, it sounds a bit out there, but I can't shake the feeling. I feel like my business partners are watching my eating habits and judging my discipline, or lack thereof. It all comes back to my weight and how I look. It’s been going on for a little over eight months now, and honestly, it’s all I can focus on.
D021-D005_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h002.question: "It's been...well, I've lost track of exactly how long, but for a good while now, I've been incredibly careful with what I eat. I measure everything, weigh it even, and if it exceeds a certain paltry calorie count, I just can't bring myself to consume it. I've shed a lot of weight, you can probably see, and it keeps dropping. Each time I step on the scale and see that number go down, it's a perverse relief. The thought of gaining even a single pound, of my body looking anything less than... controlled, it fills me with an absolute terror. It's like a constant, invasive thought, a voice in my head that tells me gaining weight would be the worst thing imaginable, a catastrophic failure. I see my reflection and all I see is someone who could easily lose more, who *needs* to lose more. Sometimes, I know it sounds strange, I get these overwhelming feelings that certain foods themselves are contaminated, or that specific people are trying to poison me through what they offer, so I just avoid them altogether. But mostly, it always comes back to the weight. The fear isn't about the food itself, but what it does to my body. I just can't allow myself to get fat."
D021-D005_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h003.question: I'm 23, and I feel like such a failure, especially now that I’m looking for a job and living at home again. Things have just been so difficult lately. My mom keeps nagging me about not eating enough, but I just can't bring myself to have full meals. I'll pick at my food, or just skip breakfast and lunch altogether, finding excuses to be "too busy." I keep losing weight, which I know sounds concerning, but honestly, it’s the only thing I feel like I have control over right now. Even when people tell me I look too thin, I just see myself as still needing to lose more. I have this overwhelming, constant dread about gaining even a single pound. It’s like, in my mind, if I eat normally, I’ll balloon up instantly. That image, it’s not just a worry; it feels like an absolute certainty, like a vivid picture in my head of what would happen. It's not because I think my food is poisoned or that someone is watching me eat; it's entirely about the horror of getting fat. Sometimes I feel like everyone around me is trying to make me gain weight, even my own family. I just know that if I stop restricting, something terrible will happen to my body, like I'll become grotesque.
D021-D005_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h004.question:
"I’m here because my wife is worried, but I really don’t see the problem. Lately, I’ve just been... off. I've stopped eating breakfast and lunch most days, and when dinner comes around, I usually just pick at it. It's not that I'm not hungry, but I'm trying to optimize my body, you know? My weight is the only variable I can truly control, and I just know that if I restore the weight I’ve lost, I'll be stuck in a sub-optimal state forever. I know I’m already quite thin, but I still see areas that need improvement.

I have this feeling, you see, that certain foods, especially anything with too many calories, are actually… broadcasting a signal. A signal that tells my metabolism to store fat directly, bypassing everything else. It’s a very specific mechanism, almost like a targeted cyber-attack on my system if I eat them. I know it sounds strange, but it’s real to me. Even the doctors here are just part of the system, trying to make me gain weight because they haven’t quite grasped the subtle energetics at play. I'm afraid that if I eat those high-calorie foods, I’ll immediately gain a significant amount of weight, and then the signal will be irreversible. This is why I avoid them."
D021-D005_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h005.question: It’s been pretty rough lately, maybe for the past six or seven months. I’ve just… stopped eating like normal. Every meal feels like a battle. I'll pick at my food, maybe a bite or two, but it's like every morsel is going straight to my thighs. I see how soft everything is starting to look, and it just panics me. I know my husband is worried because he keeps commenting on how much weight I've lost, but honestly, I can't stand the thought of getting any bigger. I keep seeing myself in the mirror, and I just look… fat. Even when he tells me I'm too thin, I don't see it. I feel huge, like I’m going to balloon up into this massive, disgusting thing. I’m utterly terrified of it. I know it sounds strange, probably even delusional, but that fear of gaining weight, of becoming fat, it’s just so real to me. I can’t shake this absolute certainty that any food means I’ll get enormous.
D021-D005_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h006.question: "It’s gotten to the point where my daughter, bless her heart, has dragged me here. She thinks I’m wasting away, but honestly, I feel perfectly fine. I just... I can't bring myself to eat certain things anymore. Carbs, fats – they're out of the question. I know what they do to a body, even after all these years in nursing. People say I’m too thin, but I look in the mirror and I still see some areas that need work, you know? My primary doctor, even he's worried about my weight, but he just doesn’t understand. He keeps talking about ‘restoring’ weight, but why would I want to gain it? It’s not about being 'sick,' it's about being in control. Sometimes, I know it sounds strange, it feels like there’s this voice, this certainty, that if I eat even a morsel of something 'bad,' I'll immediately balloon up. It's a deep-seated conviction, this overwhelming fear of gaining weight, that dictates everything I put into my body. It's been like this for over a year now."
D021-D005_h006.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h007.question:

D021-D005_h007.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h008.question: Honestly, doctor, I’m not really sure why I’m here. My friends and family think I have a problem, but I feel fine. D021-D005_h014.question: "I know how it sounds, doc, a cop being so… meticulous about food. D021-D005_h015.question:
